findings.title: Stacked items are off by a few pixels (×2)
findings.evidence: div.inline-block and div.inline-block are stacked but their left edges differ by 2.1px.
findings.fix: Give both the same left margin/padding, or put them in the same column container.

findings.title: One h2 is a different size from the other 6
findings.evidence: “Ask PostHog anything” is 24px; the other h2s are 30px (24px ×1, 30px ×6). Same semantic level should get the same treatment.
findings.fix: Pick one size for h2 and set it once in CSS. If one of these is really a sub-heading, change its tag instead of its size.
findings.citation: UICrit: elements at the same level of hierarchy should get similar graphic treatment (Duan et al., UIST '24)

findings.title: 5 different corner radii on panels
findings.evidence: Radii in use on ≥80px panels: 4px, 6px, 8px, 10px, 20px. A system usually needs two or three.
findings.fix: Define --radius-sm / --radius-md / --radius-lg tokens and use only those.

findings.title: Head is missing: <title>, canonical, favicon
findings.evidence: No JSON-LD structured data either, so AI search engines have nothing to cite. One h1, good.
findings.fix: Ten minutes of <head> work: title under 60 chars, canonical URL, lang attribute, favicon, and an Organization or WebSite JSON-LD block.

findings.title: Raster buried under a wash or opacity (×3)
findings.evidence: “raster background at opacity 0” · “raster background at opacity 0” · “raster background at opacity 0”
findings.fix: A background image under a near-opaque gradient wash, or a raster on an element at near-zero opacity, never reaches the screen: the page shows the wash, and the produced texture or photo ships as a compliance token. Let the material show (a tint under 0.9 alpha, a blend mode, an opacity you can see) or remove the file.

findings.title: Nested cards (×8)
findings.evidence: “Card inside card (div)” · “Card inside card (div)” · “Card inside card (div)”
findings.fix: Cards inside cards create visual noise and excessive depth. Flatten the hierarchy — use spacing, typography, and dividers instead of nesting containers.

findings.title: Gradient text
findings.fix: Gradient text is decorative rather than meaningful — a common AI tell, especially on headings and metrics. Use solid colors for text.

findings.title: Side-tab accent border (×3)
findings.evidence: “.vac-app .vac-developer-theme .vac-event-choice[aria-pressed=true] — inset box-shadow 3px stripe (left)” · “.vac-booking-checklist li[data-state=current] — inset box-shadow 3px stripe (left)” · “.vac-filter-comparison-row[aria-pressed=true] — inset box-shadow 3px stripe (left)”
findings.fix: Thick colored border on one side of a card — the most recognizable tell of AI-generated UIs. Use a subtler accent or remove it entirely.

findings.title: Glowing shadow accents
findings.fix: Colored glow shadows — a zero-offset chromatic halo (box- or text-shadow) on any background, or any colored blurred shadow on a dark background — are the default "cool" look of AI-generated UIs. Use neutral elevation shadows and subtle, purposeful lighting instead.

findings.title: Radial-gradient background halo
findings.fix: A chromatic radial-gradient wash — saturated at the center, fading to transparent — used as a decorative background glow on a dark page. Same tell as glowing shadows, drawn with a gradient instead of a shadow. Ground the surface with a solid or subtly shifted background instead.

findings.title: Social proof with no source (1)
findings.evidence: “Join 500,000+ teams”. Round numbers of users, 4.9/5 ratings and 99.9% uptime on a new product are the template's defaults.
findings.fix: Use a number you can link to, or none. One true sentence beats three impressive ones.

findings.title: Above-the-fold is visually busy
findings.evidence: Quadtree decomposition of the first screen (text and photos masked out) needs 1240 leaves (calm pages run 50–250; busy ones 600+). Whitespace share 30%, text covers 36% of the viewport.
findings.fix: Remove one thing from the first screen. Reinecke's data says people rate low- and medium-complexity pages the same and punish high complexity; the gain is all in cutting, not adding.
findings.citation: Reinecke et al. CHI 2013; Tuch et al.: complexity drives the 50ms impression

findings.title: h3 headings render at 2 different sizes
findings.evidence: “What can I help you with?” is 21px while “Set up for free” is 18px (1.14×). Sizes seen: 18px ×1, 21px ×1. Same semantic level should get the same treatment.
findings.fix: Pick one size for h3 and set it once in CSS. If one of these is really a sub-heading, change its tag instead of its size.
findings.citation: UICrit: elements at the same level of hierarchy should get similar graphic treatment (Duan et al., UIST '24)

findings.title: 11 elements animating at rest
findings.evidence: Keyframes in use: rough-notation-dash, grow, grow-sm, slideIn. Motion on everything is tell #4.
findings.fix: Animate the one thing you want the eye to go to. Everything else should hold still.

findings.title: “Whether you're X or Y” (1)
findings.evidence: “Whether you're analyzing customer usage or directing AI”
findings.fix: Pick the one audience you actually built this for and address them.

findings.title: 7 status dots on the page
findings.evidence: Coloured dots attached to labels where a word would say more.

findings.title: The 2026 “tasteful default”: cream background + sage/teal accent
findings.evidence: Body background rgb(238, 239, 233), 23 green/teal accents. This is the look the previous wave of anti-slop advice converged on, and the fastest-rising tell in the Reddit corpus: it reads as “AI tried to be tasteful”.
findings.fix: Nothing here is wrong in isolation. Make one choice that isn't the default: a background that isn't cream, a typeface with a point of view, or an accent pulled from your actual subject (a photo, a logo, a place).

findings.title: Only 30% of the first screen is breathing room
findings.evidence: Pixels close to the page background make up less than a third of the viewport.
findings.fix: Widen margins and loosen section padding; comprehension measurably improves when content is framed by empty space (Lin 2004).

findings.title: Repeating-gradient stripes
findings.fix: Repeating-gradient stripes used as surface decoration are a recurring generated-UI signature. Reach for a deliberate texture or leave the surface plain.
